latin: Illius naturae quae est orizon temporis et aeternitatis propria est magia, inde est petenda per modos debitos, notos sapientibus.
latin_note: The apparatus records a 1487 variant, 'per modos debitos notus', for the copy-text's 'notos' (farmer1998:25385).
translation: To that nature which is the horizon of time and eternity, magic properly belongs; from it, magic is to be sought by the due methods, known to the wise.
translation_note: 'orizon' is kept as in the neighboring theses 9>16 and 9>18, which place natures at the same kind of threshold but assign them, respectively, to the magus's proximity alone and to Cabala (farmer1998:25354; farmer1998:25362).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch17, from Latin at farmer1998:25358
doctrine: This is the middle term of the 'horizon' triad begun at 9>16 and completed at 9>18; it assigns magic, as opposed to the Cabala assigned in 9>18, as the discipline proper to the nature standing at the horizon of time and eternity (farmer1998:25358).
historiography: Mandosio quotes this thesis's Latin alongside 9>16 and 9>18 as Concl. mag. 16-18 in Pico's 1998 edition, page 500 (mandosio2012:559).
not_established: Farmer records no separate explanatory note on this thesis beyond its place among the numbered magic conclusions (research-packets/own_9_017.md).
not established by the sources consulted
